findings.evidence: PinAction.lean:134 `theorem neg_one_mem_spinGroup_of_isUnit (Q : QuadraticForm R M) (v : M) (hvQ : IsUnit (Q v))`; Kernel.lean:300-325 the `NegOne` section carries no `FiniteDimensional` and no kernel hypothesis (`variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Module K M]` at L292, with `[Nontrivial M] (hQ : Q.Nondegenerate)` per declaration), and its proof body calls only `neg_one_mem_spinGroup_of_isUnit`.
findings.fix: Move `neg_one_mem_spinGroup`, `negOneSpin`, `coe_negOneSpin` into PinAction.lean immediately after `neg_one_mem_spinGroup_of_isUnit` (adding `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.QuadraticForm.Radical` and `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.BilinearForm.Properties` there and a `Field K` section), leaving Kernel.lean with `negOneSpin_mem_ker_spinToSpecialOrthogonal`, `mem_ker_spinToSpecialOrthogonal_iff`, and `card_ker_spinToSpecialOrthogonal`. Keeping the whole `-1` API in one file is the requirement; PinAction.lean is the earliest file where both `unitι` and `spinGroup` are in scope.
findings.issue: The `NegOne` section (`neg_one_mem_spinGroup` L300, `negOneSpin` L317, `coe_negOneSpin` L323) is public Spin-group structure that never mentions the kernel and depends on no later theory — only on `neg_one_mem_spinGroup_of_isUnit` (PinAction.lean:134, added by this same PR) plus nondegeneracy. Putting the generic lemma in PinAction.lean and its immediate specialization plus the packaged element in a file named `Kernel.lean` splits one API across two files and hides `-1 ∈ Spin(Q)` where nobody looking for it will search.

summary: The new file and its imports are correctly placed, but the canonical `-1` Spin element API is split across two files: the generic membership lemma went to PinAction.lean while its specialization and the packaged element stayed in the kernel file, where they do not belong.
